selector_payload.selection_rule: Candidates are pre-ranked by three equal physical metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1 is the most physically reliable candidate. Use the highest-ranked candidate that also satisfies the user's exact material formula, state and source constraints. Never replace SiO with SiO2 or another stoichiometry.

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests a spectral-selective absorber design using recalled thin-film optics principles: a thin Cr absorption layer positioned near the incident side for visible absorption, backed by a HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave-like stack for NIR reflection on an Al substrate. The route varies individual layer thicknesses while keeping the 14-layer topology fixed. Prior knowledge includes interference stack behavior, thin-metal absorption, and antireflection principles. I would have wanted to look up measured Cr optical constants in the 400-2000 nm range, typical deposition thickness tolerances for Cr, and published spectral-selective coating architectures for validation.

routes.title: Thin-Cr Absorption Layer with Dielectric NIR-Reflector Stack on Al Substrate
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A thin Cr layer (5-30 nm) positioned after a top SiO2 antireflection layer, backed by 5 HfO2/SiO2 pairs and a bottom HfO2 layer on Al, can achieve high visible absorptance while maintaining high NIR reflectance through interference-enhanced absorption in the visible and constructive reflection in the NIR.
routes.design_principle: Recalled thin-film optics: quarter-wave dielectric stacks create high-reflection bands centered at their design wavelength; thin lossy metal layers provide absorption while remaining partially transparent for interference effects; a top dielectric layer can reduce front-surface reflection in the target absorption band. The Al substrate provides inherent NIR reflectivity that the stack enhances.
routes.proposed_topology: Air / SiO2(1) / Cr(2) / HfO2(3) / SiO2(4) / HfO2(5) / SiO2(6) / HfO2(7) / SiO2(8) / HfO2(9) / SiO2(10) / HfO2(11) / SiO2(12) / HfO2(13) / HfO2(14) / Al substrate
soft_objectives: keep total layer count at 14 (within 20-layer constraint)
manufacturing_considerations: Total 14 layers is within the 20-layer limit
Cr layer should be thin enough for uniform deposition (typically 5-30 nm is achievable)
Dielectric layers in 50-120 nm range are standard for visible-NIR coatings
No layer thickness should exceed 200 nm to avoid stress and adhesion issues
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks with alternating high/low index dielectrics produce high reflection bands centered near the quarter-wave wavelength
Recalled: Thin metal layers (5-30 nm) can provide significant absorption while remaining partially transparent for interference
Recalled: A single dielectric layer on top of a metal can act as an antireflection coating at specific wavelengths
Recalled: Al substrate has high intrinsic reflectance in the NIR, which a dielectric stack can enhance
Recalled: HfO2 has higher refractive index than SiO2 in the visible-NIR range, suitable for high-low pairs
expected_advantages: Cr positioned near the incident side captures visible light before it reaches the reflective stack
Dielectric pairs behind Cr reflect NIR back through Cr, giving a second absorption opportunity for any NIR that penetrates
Top SiO2 layer reduces front-surface reflection in the visible band
14 layers leaves margin within the 20-layer constraint for potential iteration
known_risks: Cr optical constants (n, k) in 400-2000 nm range are recalled approximately; actual values from the material registry may differ and affect absorption performance
The exact position of Cr (layer 2) is a hypothesis; optimal position might be deeper in the stack
Quarter-wave thicknesses for NIR reflection are estimated from recalled refractive indices; actual optimal thicknesses may differ
No polarization or angle specification in the request; I assume normal incidence unpolarized light, which may not match application conditions
Cr layer uniformity at 5-30 nm thickness is a manufacturing concern that I cannot verify from memory
The 14-layer topology is fixed; if performance is inadequate, the route cannot add layers without becoming a different axis
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 14-layer planar multilayer stack on aluminum substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence from incident side: SiO2 (Lemarchand) layer 1, Cr (Rakic-LD) layer 2, HfO2 layer 3, SiO2 (Lemarchand) layer 4, HfO2 layer 5, SiO2 (Lemarchand) layer 6, HfO2 layer 7, SiO2 (Lemarchand) layer 8, HfO2 layer 9, SiO2 (Lemarchand) layer 10, HfO2 layer 11, SiO2 (Lemarchand) layer 12, HfO2 layer 13, HfO2 layer 14, then Al (Rakic-LD) substrate. All 14 layer thicknesses are optimizable variables. Wavelength bands: 400-700 nm (target high absorptance, low reflectance), 700-2000 nm (target high reflectance). Incidence: normal, unpolarized. Materials: SiO2 (Lemarchand), hfo2, Cr (Rakic-LD), Al (Rakic-LD) as named in material catalog. Total layer count fixed at 14. Objective: maximize absorptance in 400-700 nm band while maximizing reflectance in 700-2000 nm band.
